papers.title: Validation of sample pooling for high-throughput RT-qPCR subtyping of avian influenza A(H5)
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) is a global health threat due to its high historical virulence and increasing mammalian host range, as demonstrated by the 2024–2025 outbreak among U.S. dairy cattle, with 71 confirmed human infections. While human-to-human transmission has not yet been documented, limited pre-existing human immunity, and uncertainty about evolutionary barriers to human infection make H5N1 a potential pandemic threat. Expanding testing capacity for H5N1 beyond its currently limited scope would be critical for response to potential outbreaks. Thus, we developed and validated a dual-target reverse transcription PCR assay for H5 subtyping of pooled influenza A-positive samples. The assay targets two regions of the hemagglutinin (HA) gene of influenza A(H5). Using contrived samples containing inactivated bovine H5N1 virus, we determined the assay’s 95% lower limit of detection for individual samples (58 copies/mL; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 50 to 66 copies/mL) and eight-sample pools (2,465 copies/mL; 95% CI: 1,969 to 3,756 copies/mL). The assay demonstrated 100% positive percent agreement, detecting H5 in all contrived H5-positive pools (32/32 pools; 95% CI: 89.1% to 100.0%) where the contrived positive samples ranged from 500,000 to 3,906 copies/mL. We observed 100% negative percent agreement in H5-negative, influenza A-positive pools (32/32; 95% CI: 89.1% to 100.0%). Though sample pooling reduced analytical sensitivity, contrived samples with H5 virus present at levels typically found in human respiratory infections were detected in eight-sample pools. This approach has the potential to increase testing capacity for influenza A (H5) while maintaining adequate sensitivity, enhancing preparedness for potential outbreaks. IMPORTANCE Avian influenza A(H5N1) poses a potential pandemic threat. H5N1 testing capacity is currently limited. We validated an influenza A (H5) subtyping RT-qPCR for testing pooled samples to increase capacity. The assay displays adequate analytical sensitivity to detect clinical respiratory infections based on prior human cases. This proactive assay validation enhances outbreak preparedness.

papers.title: Cellular tropism of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses in human respiratory and bovine mammary epithelial cells
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The recent introduction and spread of HPAI A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to U.S. dairy cattle demonstrate their ability to adapt to new mammalian hosts. Although multiple A(H5N1) genotypes have caused human infections, only two clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes (B3.13 and D1.1) have been detected in cattle, suggesting clade- or genotype-specific tropism. Understanding how these viruses replicate in human airway and bovine mammary epithelial cells is important for assessing viral evolution, mammalian adaptation, and associated public health risks. Here, we characterized replication kinetics and immune gene expression in human bronchial epithelial (Calu-3) cells and bovine mammary epithelial (MAC-T) cells infected with A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b human isolates representing the B3.13, D1.1, and B3.2 genotypes, an A(H5N1) clade 1 virus, and an A(H1N1)pdm09 strain. All viruses replicated efficiently in Calu-3 cells, although replication was delayed at 33°C compared to 37°C. Clade 2.3.4.4b viruses induced moderate expression of type I interferon and proinflammatory response in Calu-3 cells, but at lower levels than the A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H5N1) clade 1 strains. Replication and immune activation varied markedly among clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes in MAC-T cells. B3.13 viruses achieved higher titers and triggered stronger induction of innate immune response genes than other A(H5N1) genotypes or clades. These findings indicate genotype- and cell type–specific differences in replication and host responses, with B3.13 showing enhanced tropism in bovine mammary cells, consistent with adaptation that may elevate zoonotic risk. Our results highlight the value of comparative studies across host cell types and diverse viral isolates to inform risk assessments for emerging influenza viruses. IMPORTANCE Influenza A viruses cross species barriers through a combination of factors, including the ability to bind to and infect permissive cells, replicate efficiently, and modulate host immune responses. Since 2024, A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have continued to evolve, infecting a broad range of avian and mammalian species, including cattle in the United States, and causing sporadic human infections. Here, we evaluated a panel of A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses isolated from humans to assess their replication and host responses in two relevant mammalian cell types: human bronchial epithelial cells and bovine mammary gland epithelial cells. While all genotypes replicated efficiently in human bronchial epithelial cells, only B3.13 viruses showed strong replication and broad host response induction in bovine mammary epithelial cells. These results underscore variation in evolution, tissue tropism, and host adaptation among A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses and highlight the need for continued surveillance and close monitoring of B3.13 genotype viruses.

papers.title_zh: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) A(H5N1) 分支 2.3.4.4b 病毒在人呼吸道和牛乳腺上皮细胞中的细胞向性
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT The recent introduction and spread of HPAI A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses to U.S. dairy cattle demonstrate their ability to adapt to new mammalian hosts. Although multiple A(H5N1) genotypes have caused human infections, only two clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes (B3.13 and D1.1) have been detected in cattle, suggesting clade- or genotype-specific tropism. Understanding how these viruses replicate in human airway and bovine mammary epithelial cells is important for assessing viral evolution, mammalian adaptation, and associated public health risks. Here, we characterized replication kinetics and immune gene expression in human bronchial epithelial (Calu-3) cells and bovine mammary epithelial (MAC-T) cells infected with A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b human isolates representing the B3.13, D1.1, and B3.2 genotypes, an A(H5N1) clade 1 virus, and an A(H1N1)pdm09 strain. All viruses replicated efficiently in Calu-3 cells, although replication was delayed at 33°C compared to 37°C. Clade 2.3.4.4b viruses induced moderate expression of type I interferon and proinflammatory response in Calu-3 cells, but at lower levels than the A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H5N1) clade 1 strains. Replication and immune activation varied markedly among clade 2.3.4.4b genotypes in MAC-T cells. B3.13 viruses achieved higher titers and triggered stronger induction of innate immune response genes than other A(H5N1) genotypes or clades. These findings indicate genotype- and cell type–specific differences in replication and host responses, with B3.13 showing enhanced tropism in bovine mammary cells, consistent with adaptation that may elevate zoonotic risk. Our results highlight the value of comparative studies across host cell types and diverse viral isolates to inform risk assessments for emerging influenza viruses. IMPORTANCE Influenza A viruses cross species barriers through a combination of factors, including the ability to bind to and infect permissive cells, replicate efficiently, and modulate host immune responses. Since 2024, A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have continued to evolve, infecting a broad range of avian and mammalian species, including cattle in the United States, and causing sporadic human infections. Here, we evaluated a panel of A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses isolated from humans to assess their replication and host responses in two relevant mammalian cell types: human bronchial epithelial cells and bovine mammary gland epithelial cells. While all genotypes replicated efficiently in human bronchial epithelial cells, only B3.13 viruses showed strong replication and broad host response induction in bovine mammary epithelial cells. These results underscore variation in evolution, tissue tropism, and host adaptation among A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses and highlight the need for continued surveillance and close monitoring of B3.13 genotype viruses.

papers.title: Xenobiotics at environmental levels modulate influenza virus replication in a lineage- and subtype-dependent manner in vitro.
papers.abstract: The influence of environmentally relevant concentrations of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-active pollutants on low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV) replication remains poorly resolved, particularly under realistic co-exposure scenarios. Here, we quantified how single and mixed AhR agonists modulate replication of multiple LPAIV subtypes in avian fibroblasts at field-relevant concentrations. Chicken (DF-1) and duck (CCL-141) fibroblasts were exposed to 9-chlorophenanthrene (0.1-50 nM), PCB126 (0.01-10 nM), and TCDD (0.001-1 nM), with or without the endogenous AhR ligand 6-formylindolo[3,2-b]carbazole (FICZ), and subsequently infected with four LPAIV subtypes (H16N3, H9N2, H7N3, H5N3). Viral replication was quantified by qPCR (ΔCt). Factorial models emphasized host lineage × virus subtype interactions and mixture-versus-single comparisons across a shared concentration window. Host lineage × virus subtype interactions explained the largest share of variance. Single-agent effects were highly context-dependent; statistically supported antiviral activity was observed only for PCB126 in DF-1 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 0.006). In contrast, a three-compound pollutant mixture significantly enhanced replication in CCL-141 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 3.8 × 10^-4), whereas this supported trend was not observed with FICZ co-exposure. Within the tested environmentally plausible concentration window, concentration-matched Highest Single Agent comparisons more often yielded mixture responses below the strongest matched single-agent response among the evaluated comparisons. Within the tested concentration window, responses were graded and lacked clear thresholds. Overall, AhR-active xenobiotics can tune LPAIV replication in a host- and subtype-specific manner, highlighting the need for mixture-aware, context-dependent ecological infection-risk assessment.

Chicken (DF-1) and duck (CCL-141) fibroblasts were exposed to 9-chlorophenanthrene (0.1-50 nM), PCB126 (0.01-10 nM), and TCDD (0.001-1 nM), with or without the endogenous AhR ligand 6-formylindolo[3,2-b]carbazole (FICZ), and subsequently infected with four LPAIV subtypes (H16N3, H9N2, H7N3, H5N3). Viral replication was quantified by qPCR (ΔCt). Factorial models emphasized host lineage × virus subtype interactions and mixture-versus-single comparisons across a shared concentration window. Host lineage × virus subtype interactions explained the largest share of variance. Single-agent effects were highly context-dependent; statistically supported antiviral activity was observed only for PCB126 in DF-1 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 0.006). In contrast, a three-compound pollutant mixture significantly enhanced replication in CCL-141 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 3.8 × 10^-4), whereas this supported trend was not observed with FICZ co-exposure. Within the tested environmentally plausible concentration window, concentration-matched Highest Single Agent comparisons more often yielded mixture responses below the strongest matched single-agent response among the evaluated comparisons. Within the tested concentration window, responses were graded and lacked clear thresholds. Overall, AhR-active xenobiotics can tune LPAIV replication in a host- and subtype-specific manner, highlighting the need for mixture-aware, context-dependent ecological infection-risk assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how environmentally relevant concentrations of AhR-active pollutants affect replication of low-pathogenic avian influenza viruses (LPAIV) in avian fibroblasts. The research highlights the complex interactions between host lineage, virus subtype, and pollutant exposure, emphasizing the need for context-dependent ecological risk assessments. The study used factorial models to analyze host lineage × virus subtype interactions and mixture-versus-single comparisons. Results showed that single-agent effects were highly context-dependent, with PCB126 demonstrating antiviral activity in DF-1 cells infected with H7N3. In contrast, a three-compound pollutant mixture significantly enhanced replication in CCL-141 cells infected with H7N3. The findings suggest that AhR-active xenobiotics can modulate LPAIV replication in a host- and subtype-specific manner, underscoring the importance of considering pollutant mixtures in ecological and public health assessments.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 阶乘模型强调 宿主 谱系 × 病毒亚型相互作用以及共享浓度窗口内的混合物与单一比较。

papers.title: Application and evaluation of a migratory exposure risk for avian influenza in Ireland (2013–2025)
papers.abstract: Avian Influenza (AI) is a zoonotic virus infecting wild birds and poultry. AI can be spread via wild bird migration, especially by waterfowl. On the island of Ireland, most outbreaks in poultry are linked to wild bird contact. Therefore, predicting the exposure to AI through wild birds could help with directing measures and disease preparedness. We retrospectively applied a stochastic simulation model to estimate the migration-mediated exposure risk of AI in Ireland from 2013 to 2025, based on wild bird short distance movements and seasonal migration. Migration routes include the continent of Europe and Iceland as possible source populations and entry routes of AI, given known bird migration pathways. The model estimated the yearly migration-mediated exposure risk and identified peaks in 2020, 2021, and a particular high emerging peak in autumn of 2025. There was a temporal correlation between migration-mediated exposure risk per month with observed outbreaks. However, the predicted migration-mediated exposure risk for the model resulted in consistently higher number of modelled “incursions” relative to the number of outbreaks observed – indicating a need for migration-mediated exposure risk models to be linked to a within-island epidemic model. Preferably one that includes the probability of subsequent infections and detection. This study highlights a benefit for the application of locally tailored risk models, but also the need for future work to collate and analyse data in “real-time” to improve such tools.
papers.journal: Preventive Veterinary Medicine Regional Studies and Reports

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the migration-mediated exposure risk of avian influenza in Ireland from 2013 to 2025 using a stochastic simulation model. The research aimed to understand how wild bird movements contribute to AI outbreaks in poultry, as most outbreaks are linked to wild bird contact. The model considered migration routes from Europe and Iceland, based on known bird migration pathways. It identified peaks in exposure risk in 2020, 2021, and autumn 2025, with a temporal correlation between exposure risk and observed outbreaks. However, the model predicted more incursions than actual outbreaks, suggesting the need for integration with within-island epidemic models. The study emphasizes the importance of locally tailored risk models and the necessity for real-time data analysis to enhance disease preparedness. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on a retrospective model and do not include detailed limitations.

papers.title: Development, Immunogenicity and Protective Efficacy of an Associated Inactivated Vaccine Against Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza and Newcastle Disease in Chickens
papers.abstract: Background: The simultaneous circulation of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N8 (clade 2.3.4.4b) and virulent Newcastle disease virus (NDV) genotype VII creates a cumulative risk for the poultry industry, rendering monovalent vaccination insufficient. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a combined inactivated vaccine against AIV H5N8 and NDV genotype VII based on local endemic strains. Methods: The vaccine was formulated as a water-in-oil emulsion (30:70) using MontanideTM ISA 78 VG. Evaluation included physicochemical characterization, safety assessment in chickens, immunogenicity evaluation via the hemagglutination inhibition (HI) test, and protective efficacy following challenge with virulent isolates. Results: The formulation demonstrated high stability and complete safety without adverse reactions. By 28 days post-immunization, the vaccine induced a robust, balanced humoral response with antibody titers reaching 9.10 ± 0.23 log2 against NDV and 9.00 ± 0.26 log2 against AIV, indicating no antigenic interference. Upon challenge, the vaccinated group exhibited 100% clinical protection and survival, compared to 100% mortality in controls. Furthermore, vaccination significantly reduced viral shedding, limiting horizontal spread. Conclusions: The developed combined inactivated vaccine demonstrates high safety, stability, and protective efficacy. It represents a promising candidate for comprehensive specific prophylaxis in endemic regions, effectively limiting horizontal pathogen transmission and mitigating economic losses in poultry production.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5N8(进化枝 2.3.4.4b)和强毒新城疫病毒 (NDV) 基因型 VII 的同时传播给家禽业造成累积风险,导致单价 疫苗接种 不足。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在开发和评估基于当地流行毒株的针对 AIV H5N8 和 NDV 基因型 VII 的组合灭活 疫苗。评估包括理化特性、鸡的安全性评估、通过血凝抑制(HI)测试的免疫原性评估以及强毒分离株攻击后的保护功效。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 MontanideTM ISA 78 VG 将 疫苗 配制为油包水乳液 (30:70)。
elements_zh.main_results: 免疫后 ​​28 天,疫苗 诱导了强烈、平衡的体液反应,针对 NDV 的抗体滴度达到 9.10 ± 0.23 log2,针对 AIV 的抗体滴度达到 9.00 ± 0.26 log2,表明没有抗原干扰。攻击后,接种组表现出 100% 的临床保护和存活率,而对照组的 死亡率 为 100%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 所开发的组合灭活疫苗具有较高的安全性、稳定性和保护功效。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 它是流行地区全面特异性预防的有前途的候选药物,可有效限制水平病原体 传播 并减轻家禽生产的经济损失。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.title_zh: 相关灭活 疫苗 针对 高致病性禽流感 和鸡新城疫的开发、免疫原性和保护功效
papers.source_body_en: Background: The simultaneous circulation of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N8 (clade 2.3.4.4b) and virulent Newcastle disease virus (NDV) genotype VII creates a cumulative risk for the poultry industry, rendering monovalent vaccination insufficient. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a combined inactivated vaccine against AIV H5N8 and NDV genotype VII based on local endemic strains. Methods: The vaccine was formulated as a water-in-oil emulsion (30:70) using MontanideTM ISA 78 VG. Evaluation included physicochemical characterization, safety assessment in chickens, immunogenicity evaluation via the hemagglutination inhibition (HI) test, and protective efficacy following challenge with virulent isolates. Results: The formulation demonstrated high stability and complete safety without adverse reactions. By 28 days post-immunization, the vaccine induced a robust, balanced humoral response with antibody titers reaching 9.10 ± 0.23 log2 against NDV and 9.00 ± 0.26 log2 against AIV, indicating no antigenic interference. Upon challenge, the vaccinated group exhibited 100% clinical protection and survival, compared to 100% mortality in controls. Furthermore, vaccination significantly reduced viral shedding, limiting horizontal spread. Conclusions: The developed combined inactivated vaccine demonstrates high safety, stability, and protective efficacy. It represents a promising candidate for comprehensive specific prophylaxis in endemic regions, effectively limiting horizontal pathogen transmission and mitigating economic losses in poultry production.

papers.title: Conflicts hinder research into animal movements.
papers.abstract: Satellite tracking has revolutionized our understanding of animal migration, yet its reliability increasingly depends on the geopolitical stability of the regions frequented by wildlife. Here, we show that military-induced interference with global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) during ongoing conflicts in Eastern Europe has severely compromised the accuracy of global positioning systems (GPS)-based tracking data for black-headed gulls (Chroicocephalus ridibundus). In 2024-2025, GPS trajectories revealed erratic, low-quality, and geographically implausible positions coinciding with known zones of electronic warfare. These inaccuracies hinder efforts to locate breeding colonies, identify key stopover habitats, and assess disease transmission risks posed by migratory birds, particularly for zoonoses such as highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1. Our findings illustrate how modern conflicts now extend their impact into ecological research infrastructures, calling for systematic correction methods and international coordination to safeguard the robustness of movement ecology studies and One Health models in a geopolitically unstable world.

papers.abstract: Abstract The global risk of avian influenza outbreaks has increased significantly in recent years, posing substantial threats to both the poultry industry and public health due to frequent human infection cases. Occupational groups within the poultry industry face particularly high infection risks because of prolonged close contact with poultry. This study aimed to identify differences in knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding avian influenza among various occupational categories, pinpoint weaknesses in prevention and control, and provide scientific evidence to support targeted intervention strategies. We conducted a cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling among 1,362 individuals engaged in poultry-related occupations in Anhui, Sichuan, and Guangxi provinces, China, from May to July 2025. Data on avian influenza-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) were collected through electronic questionnaires. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS 27.0, employing descriptive statistics, chi-square tests for group comparisons, and multivariate logistic regression to identify factors associated with KAP levels. A total of 1,194 valid questionnaires were collected. The overall KAP qualification rate among survey participants was 48.16%, with knowledge awareness being the lowest (33.84%), the positive attitude rate was 83.42%, and the positive practice rate was 41.46%. Multivariate analysis identified distinct factors influencing knowledge, attitude, and practice. Regarding knowledge, commercial farm workers (aOR = 1.87,95%CI:1.24–2.81) and backyard farmers(aOR = 2.40,95%CI:1.37–4.21) had higher levels than live poultry market workers, with urban residents(aOR = 1.49,95%CI:1.06–2.09), higher education, and absence of chronic disease (aOR = 1.94,95%CI:1.30–2.91) also predicting better knowledge. For attitude, commercial farm workers (aOR = 3.02,95%CI:1.67–5.46) and urban residents (aOR = 2.84,95%CI:1.79–4.51) were more positive. For practice, workers in Guangxi outperformed those in Anhui (aOR = 1.72,95%CI:1.06–2.79); commercial farm workers (aOR = 7.01,95%CI:4.55–10.80) and slaughterhouse workers (aOR = 6.33,95%CI:3.63–11.05) outperformed live poultry market workers, while backyard farmers showed poorer practices (aOR = 0.40,95%CI:0.22–0.74); females exhibited better practices than males (aOR = 1.33,95% CI:1.01–1.77). Furthermore, mobile internet (59.55%) and television/radio (50.42%) were the primary sources of information across all occupational groups. The findings reveal a pattern of superficial knowledge, and positive attitudes that do not translate into effective protective practices. Live poultry market workers, backyard farmers, individuals with lower education levels, and those residing in rural areas demonstrated poorer knowledge of avian influenza, while males exhibited lower adoption rates of protective practices. These populations should be prioritized as key targets for intervention. It is recommended to implement targeted health communication through new media platforms to enhance the coverage and effectiveness of intervention measures.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 近年来,禽流感 暴发 的全球风险显着增加,人类感染病例频发,对家禽业和公众健康构成重大威胁。由于与家禽长期密切接触,家禽业的职业群体面临特别高的感染风险。本研究旨在明确不同职业类别对禽流感知识、态度和实践(KAP)的差异,查明防控薄弱环节,为有针对性的干预策略提供科学依据。我们于2025年5月至2025年7月对中国安徽、四川、广西三省从事家禽相关职业的1,362名从事家禽相关职业的个体进行了横断面调查。通过电子问卷收集了禽流感相关知识、态度和实践(KAP)数据。使用 SPSS 27.0 进行统计分析,采用描述性统计、组间比较的卡方检验以及多元逻辑回归来确定与 KAP 水平相关的因素。共回收有效问卷1194份。调查对象KAP总体合格率为48.16%,其中知识知晓率最低(33.84%),积极态度率为83.42%,积极实践率为41.46%。多变量分析确定了影响知识、态度和实践的不同因素。在知识方面,商业农场工人(aOR = 1.87,95%CI:1.24–2.81)和散养农民(aOR = 2.40,95%CI:1.37–4.21)的知识水平高于活禽市场工人,城市居民(aOR = 1.49,95%CI:1.06–2.09)、受教育程度较高、无慢性病(aOR = 1.94,95%CI:1.30–2.91)也预测了更好的知识。对于态度,商业农场工人(aOR=3.02,95%CI:1.67-5.46)和城市居民(aOR=2.84,95%CI:1.79-4.51)更为积极。就实践而言,广西工人的表现优于安徽工人(aOR = 1.72,95%CI:1.06–2.79);商业农场工人(aOR = 7.01,95%CI:4.55–10.80)和屠宰场工人(aOR = 6.33,95%CI:3.63–11.05)表现优于活禽市场工人,而散养农民的表现较差(aOR = 0.40,95%CI:0.22–0.74);女性表现出比男性更好的实践(aOR = 1.33,95% CI:1.01–1.77)。此外,移动互联网(59.55%)和电视/广播(50.42%)是所有职业群体的主要信息来源。研究结果揭示了一种肤浅的知识和积极态度的模式,这些模式并不能转化为有效的保护措施。活禽市场工作人员、散养农民、受教育程度较低的个人以及居住在农村地区的人对 禽流感 的了解较少,而男性对保护措施的采用率较低。这些人群应优先作为干预的重点目标。建议通过新媒体平台开展有针对性的健康传播,提高干预措施的覆盖面和有效性。

papers.title: The impact of acids, pH, and incubation time on avian influenza virus persistence in raw milk
papers.abstract: In March 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) clade 2.3.4.4. b H5N1 was detected in dairy cattle. Since detection, the virus has spread across 17 states, infecting more than 1000 dairy herds, causing concern for the dairy industry regarding the effects on dairy cattle, the risk associated with milk quality and production, and ultimately its risk to humans. It has been shown that pasteurization is sufficient to inactivate HPAIV, if present in milk, making it safe for human consumption. However, unpasteurized raw milk that is routinely consumed and used to make cheese, yogurt, and kefir is a public health concern. We acidified raw milk, a process that is analogous to the preliminary phase of generating fermented milk products, with acetic, propionic, lactic, or citric acid to pH 5; or acidified it with acetic acid to pH 6, 5, or 4. Each sample was subsequently spiked with low pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV) and incubated at room temperature for up to 24 h before being inoculated into 10-day old specific-pathogen-free embryonating chicken eggs. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed due to the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 in dairy cattle across 17 states, raising concerns about milk quality, production, and human health risks from unpasteurized raw milk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved acidifying raw milk with various acids to different pH levels, spiking it with low pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV), and incubating it at room temperature for up to 24 hours before inoculating into 10-day-old specific-pathogen-free embryonating chicken eggs.
analysis.methods: Samples were acidified with acetic, propionic, lactic, or citric acid to pH 5 or with acetic acid to pH 6, 5, or 4, spiked with LPAIV, incubated, and then inoculated into embryonating chicken eggs, with viability assessed daily via hemagglutination assays.
analysis.main_results: The reduction of viable virus was significantly correlated with both time and pH but not the specific type of acid tested; samples at pH 6 showed little reduction in virus viability, while acid treatment at pH 4 and 5 progressively reduced viable LPAIV levels over time.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that acid treatment, particularly at lower pH levels, can effectively inactivate LPAIV in raw milk, providing a novel approach to reduce public health risks associated with unpasteurized dairy products.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform potential interventions for reducing avian influenza virus persistence in raw milk, thereby mitigating risks to human health from unpasteurized dairy products used in fermented foods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study was conducted in a controlled laboratory setting using embryonating chicken eggs, which may not fully replicate real-world conditions in dairy processing or human consumption.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of acids, pH, and incubation time on avian influenza virus persistence in raw milk, motivated by the recent outbreak of HPAIV H5N1 in dairy cattle. Researchers acidified raw milk with various acids to different pH levels, spiked it with LPAIV, and incubated it before assessing virus viability in embryonating chicken eggs. Results showed that lower pH levels (4 and 5) significantly reduced viable virus over time, with pH 6 showing minimal effect, while the type of acid did not influence inactivation. The findings suggest that acid treatment could be a practical method to reduce avian influenza virus risks in unpasteurized dairy products, though further studies in real-world settings are needed.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于 高致病性禽流感 病毒 (HPAIV) 分支 2.3.4.4b H5N1 在 17 个州的奶牛中传播,引发了人们对未经高温消毒的原料奶的牛奶质量、生产和人类健康风险的担忧,因此需要进行这项研究。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及用各种酸将生奶酸化至不同的 pH 值,添加低致病性 禽流感 病毒 (LPAIV),并在室温下孵育长达 24 小时,然后接种到 10 日龄的无特定病原体的胚胎鸡蛋中。
elements_zh.methods: 将样品用乙酸、丙酸、乳酸或柠檬酸酸化至 pH 5,或用乙酸酸化至 pH 6、5 或 4,加入 LPAIV,孵育,然后接种到含胚鸡蛋中,每天通过血凝测定评估活力。
elements_zh.main_results: 活病毒的减少与时间和 pH 值显着相关,但与测试的酸的具体类型无关;pH 6 的样品显示病毒活力几乎没有降低,而 pH 4 和 5 的酸 治疗 随着时间的推移逐渐降低活的 LPAIV 水平。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,酸 治疗,特别是在较低 pH 水平下,可以有效灭活原料奶中的 LPAIV,为降低与未经巴氏消毒的乳制品相关的公共卫生风险提供了一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为减少原奶中 禽流感 病毒持久性的潜在干预措施提供了信息,从而减轻发酵食品中使用的未经高温消毒的乳制品对人类健康的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究是在受控实验室环境中使用胚胎鸡蛋进行的,这可能无法完全复制乳制品加工或人类消费的现实条件。

papers.title: Risk Factors, Perception, and Knowledge of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza among Poultry Handlers in Selected Live Bird Markets in Nigeria
papers.abstract: Objectives: The live bird markets (LBMs) are considered a very high-risk area for the transmission of infectious pathogens in poultry due to the large numbers of uninspected mixed poultry species of unknown disease status that are brought together. The objective was to identify gaps in knowledge, risk perception, and biosecurity practices related to highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) LBMs workers in parts of Northern Nigeria. Material and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 226 LBM workers using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire. Data on socio-demographics, poultry handling practices, biosecurity measures, knowledge, and risk perception were analyzed using descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression. Results: All respondents were male (mean age 40 ± 12.3 years). HPAI awareness was high among LBM workers (>95%); however, knowledge of its zoonotic potential was low ( 90%) of the vendors traded in multiple bird species. Forty-five percent (45%) of the vendors consider the introduction of sick birds into the market to be of low risk, while 42% perceive it as high risk for the transmission of the influenza virus. More than 70% of vendors regularly clean their stalls and cages as an important biosecurity measure. Vendors who separate sick from healthy birds were less likely to experience influenza virus transmission in the market (odds ratio [OR]: 0.214; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.073–0.630). The use of personal protective equipment and disinfection of vehicles used were associated with a reduced risk of transmission of influenza viruses within the LBM (OR: 0.534; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.298–0.953; OR: 0.584; 95% CL: 0.450–0.757), respectively. Conclusion: Despite high awareness, critical gaps in zoonotic knowledge, biosecurity lapses, and low risk perception exist. Targeted risk communication and enhanced biosecurity protocols are urgently needed to mitigate HPAI transmission in these LBMs.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过检查家禽处理者的知识、认知和生物安全实践来解决活禽市场中 禽流感 传播 的风险。由于大量未经检查、疾病状况不明的混合家禽品种聚集在一起,活禽市场被认为是家禽传染性病原体 传播 的高风险区域。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用结构化访谈问卷对尼日利亚北部部分地区的 226 名 LBM 工人进行了一项横断面研究。所有受访者均为男性(平均年龄 40 ± 12.3 岁)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用描述性统计和二元逻辑回归分析有关社会人口统计、家禽处理实践、生物安全措施、知识和风险认知的数据。
elements_zh.main_results: LBM 员工对 HPAI 的认识较高(>95%);然而,人们对其人畜共患潜力的了解还很少。百分之四十五 (45%) 的供应商认为将病禽引入市场风险较低,而 42% 的供应商认为对于流感病毒 传播 风险较高。将病禽与健康禽类分开的供应商在市场上感染流感病毒 传播 的可能性较小(比值比 [OR]:0.214;95% 置信区间 [CI]:0.073–0.630)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,尽管人们的认识很高,但人畜共患知识、生物安全失误和低风险认知方面仍存在严重差距。这项研究强调需要有针对性的风险沟通和增强的生物安全协议,以减轻这些 LBM 中的 HPAI 传播。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为有针对性的风险沟通策略和增强生物安全方案的制定提供信息,以降低活禽市场中 HPAI 传播 的风险,这对尼日利亚的公共卫生至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。证据是温和的,因为它基于自我报告的数据和描述性统计。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,尽管人们的认识很高,但人畜共患知识、生物安全失误和低风险认知方面仍存在严重差距。这项研究强调需要有针对性的风险沟通和增强的生物安全协议,以减轻这些 LBM 中的 HPAI 传播。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为有针对性的风险沟通策略和增强生物安全方案的制定提供信息,以降低活禽市场中 HPAI 传播 的风险,这对尼日利亚的公共卫生至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法确定因果关系。证据是温和的,因为它基于自我报告的数据和描述性统计。

papers.full_text: Australia has confirmed deadly H5N1 bird flu has been found in 102 wild seabirds across five states at the time of writing, including the country’s first mass death of birds. The question is no longer if this virus can harm Australian wildlife, but whether we should use every available tool to protect species most at risk. Vaccination cannot stop H5N1 spreading through wildlife. But it could prevent an outbreak from killing all of the at-risk species in an area – a tragic local extinction. Australia should begin targeted vaccination of threatened birds. It should also urgently develop a strategy for seals and sea lions, rather than waiting until thousands are dead. A policy exists, but action remains too cautious Australia has a national policy that allows emergency vaccination of rare, protected and valuable birds, including animals in zoos, sanctuaries, breeding programs and some managed wild populations. The government has also purchased an inactivated H5 vaccine – containing no live virus – and is running pilot studies in captive non-poultry birds. This is important groundwork, but not yet a public program comparable with New Zealand’s ambitious and proactive approach to vaccinate five of the country’s rarest birds before the arrival of H5N1. Australian zoos and sanctuaries have received funding to strengthen biosecurity and captive “insurance populations”. Pilot vaccinations are underway, but the government has not announced which threatened species will receive wider vaccination, where, or when. More importantly, the policy excludes non-avian (bird) species, meaning marine mammals are not considered despite their known vulnerability to H5N1. No plans have been announced to the public for Australian vaccination trials for seals or sea lions. What overseas programs show New Zealand prepared before H5N1 arrived. After species-specific trials, it began vaccinating about 300 core breeding birds of rare species, including kākāpō, takahē and black stilts. These are captive or closely managed populations whose individuals can be found, vaccinated twice and monitored. The United States acted after H5N1 killed 21 critically endangered California condors. By October 2024, 207 captive and free-flying condors had been vaccinated. The vaccine was judged safe, although two birds had treatable adverse reactions. France has conducted a vaccine trial in wild king penguin chicks on the French sub-Antarctic island of Crozet. The vaccine produced strong, virus-neutralising antibodies without detected adverse effects. These programs do not prove vaccination will prevent every infection. But it could lessen severe disease and reduce the number of animals that die in threatened populations. Which species should Australia vaccinate? Broadscale vaccination of free-ranging wildlife is unrealistic. Most H5 vaccines require two doses, and most wildlife is difficult to capture once, let alone being recaptured for a booster and blood test. The best candidates are small populations of at-risk species that are either easily accessible or already under management. For example, threatened birds in zoos or breeding centres, or small, known colonies with tracking or regular handling. On Tuesday, the Australian government released a list of at-risk species, that showed almost one-in-five Australian bird and mammal species is at high, very high or extreme risk from the virus. Five bird species are at extreme risk – the Christmas Island frigate bird, Houtman albatross, Herald petrel, imperial shag on Heard Island and imperial shag on Macquarie Island. The marine mammals most at risk are the sea lion, fur seal and elephant seal, while the Tasmanian devil and eastern quoll are the highest risk species on land. Decisions must balance extinction risk, exposure to the virus, cost, vaccine performance, whether enough animals can be reached, and whether capture would cause unacceptable stress. Vaccination must sit alongside existing biosecurity, surveillance and conservation measures – not replace them. Australia needs a seal plan H5N1 has decimated seal and sea lion populations across South America and the Southern Ocean. More than 17,000 southern elephant seal pups were killed in Argentina in 2023. An estimated 13,359 pups died at the Australian sub-Antarctic Heard Island in 2025, believed to be from the virus. Southern elephant seals were listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List in April, in part because of the catastrophic mortality caused by bird flu. It will take decades for these populations to recover. Australia’s most vulnerable seals include the endangered Australian sea lion, Australian and long-nosed fur seals, and southern elephant seals. H5N1-positive terns have already been found at Seal Bay on Kangaroo Island, home to a major Australian sea lion breeding colony. Southern elephant seals have a large breeding colony on Australia’s sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, which remains free of H5N1 at this time. There is currently no bird flu vaccine designed specifically for marine mammals. A United States trial aimed at protecting endangered Hawaiian monk seals found a vaccine developed for cattle was safe in northern elephant seals and produced measurable antibodies. This was the closest comparable species for which a safe, conditionally licensed vaccine was available. Developing and approving a separate vaccine for every wildlife species is costly and time-consuming, so conservation programs commonly adapt vaccines already approved for domestic animals. Now is the time to act Australia should identify priority seal colonies now, trial candidate vaccines in a suitable surrogate species and plan how vaccination could be deployed. We should not wait to learn how susceptible these animals are by watching more mass deaths unfold. Vaccination is not a silver bullet. But when a disease can erase years of conservation work in weeks, we should not wait for perfect certainty. It’s time to act before catastrophe.

papers.title_original: Why Australia should urgently vaccinate wildlife most at risk from H5N1 bird flu

analysis.research_question_and_background: Australia faces an urgent public-health and conservation crisis as H5N1 bird flu has caused mass mortality in wild seabirds across multiple states, raising the question whether targeted wildlife vaccination can prevent local extinctions of the most vulnerable species.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The paper is a policy analysis and commentary that synthesizes Australia’s current H5N1 situation, existing national policy, pilot vaccination efforts, and overseas programs to argue for urgent, targeted vaccination of threatened wildlife.
analysis.methods: The analysis draws on government reports of H5N1 detections and mortality, policy documents on emergency vaccination, and published accounts of overseas vaccination trials in birds and seals to assess feasibility and gaps.
analysis.main_results: Australia has confirmed H5N1 in 102 wild seabirds across five states and recorded an estimated 13,359 pup deaths at Heard Island in 2025, with five bird species and several marine mammals identified as at extreme or high risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The author interprets that vaccination cannot stop H5N1 spread but could reduce severe disease and prevent local extinctions in small, accessible populations, highlighting the need for proactive, species-specific strategies rather than waiting for mass die-offs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support immediate, targeted vaccination of the most at-risk wildlife—especially threatened birds in managed settings and priority seal colonies—while integrating vaccination with existing biosecurity, surveillance, and conservation measures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to policy analysis and overseas case reports; Australia has not yet announced which species will be vaccinated, where, or when, and broadscale wildlife vaccination remains logistically challenging.

analysis.summary_en: Australia is confronting widespread H5N1 bird flu in wild seabirds and catastrophic mortality in seals, prompting urgent debate about wildlife vaccination. The author argues that while vaccination cannot halt H5N1 spread, it could mitigate severe disease and prevent local extinctions in small, accessible populations such as threatened birds in zoos or breeding programs and priority seal colonies. Australia already has a national policy allowing emergency vaccination and has purchased an inactivated H5 vaccine, with pilot studies underway in captive non-poultry birds, but no public program comparable to New Zealand’s proactive approach has been announced. Overseas programs in New Zealand, the United States, and France demonstrate feasibility and safety in managed or closely monitored populations, though adverse reactions and logistical hurdles remain. The paper calls for immediate identification of priority seal colonies, surrogate-species vaccine trials, and deployment planning, emphasizing that vaccination must complement—not replace—existing biosecurity and conservation measures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 澳大利亚面临着紧迫的公共卫生和保护危机,因为 H5N1 禽流感已在多个州的野生海鸟中造成大规模 死亡率,这引发了一个问题:目标野生动物 死亡率 是否可以防止最脆弱物种的局部灭绝。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该文件是一份政策分析和评论,综合了澳大利亚目前的 H5N1 情况、现有国家政策、疫苗接种 试点工作以及海外计划,以主张对受威胁野生动物采取紧急、有针对性的 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.methods: 该分析借鉴了 H5N1 检测和 Z​​XQTERMQQXZ 的政府报告、紧急情况 疫苗接种 的政策文件以及已发布的海外 疫苗接种 在鸟类和海豹身上进行试验的记录,以评估可行性和差距。
elements_zh.main_results: 澳大利亚已在五个州的 102 只野生海鸟中确认了 H5N1 病毒,并记录到 2025 年赫德岛估计有 13,359 只海鸟幼崽死亡,其中 5 种鸟类和几种海洋哺乳动物被确定为处于极端或高风险中。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,疫苗接种 无法阻止 H5N1 传播,但可以减少严重疾病并防止小规模易接近人群的局部灭绝,这强调需要采取积极主动的针对物种的策略,而不是等待大规模死亡。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持对最危险的野生动物(尤其是受管理环境和优先海豹栖息地中的受威胁鸟类)立即采取有针对性的 疫苗接种,同时将 疫苗接种 与现有的生物安全、监测 和保护措施相结合。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于政策分析和海外病例报告;澳大利亚尚未宣布将在哪些物种、地点或时间接种疫苗,大规模野生动物 疫苗接种 在后勤方面仍然具有挑战性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 澳大利亚面临着紧迫的公共卫生和保护危机,因为 H5N1 禽流感已在多个州的野生海鸟中造成大规模 死亡率,这引发了一个问题:目标野生动物 死亡率 是否可以防止最脆弱物种的局部灭绝。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该文件是一份政策分析和评论,综合了澳大利亚目前的 H5N1 情况、现有国家政策、疫苗接种 试点工作以及海外计划,以主张对受威胁野生动物采取紧急、有针对性的 疫苗接种。

Home Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local En Español Edition Africa Australia Brasil Canada Canada (français) Català España Europe France Global Indonesia New Zealand United Kingdom United States Donate Skip to content Edition: United States Africa Australia Brasil Canada Canada (français) Català España Europe France Global Indonesia New Zealand United Kingdom s Donate Newsletters Become an author Sign up as a reader Sign in Academic rigor, journalistic flair Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local Auscape/Getty Why Australia should urgently vaccinate wildlife most at risk from H5N1 bird flu Published: August 5, 2026 4:09pm EDT Australia has confirmed deadly H5N1 bird flu has been found in 102 wild seabirds across five states at the time of writing, including the country’s first mass death of birds. The question is no longer if this virus can harm Australian wildlife, but whether we should use every available tool to protect species most at risk. Vaccination cannot stop H5N1 spreading through wildlife. But it could prevent an outbreak from killing all of the at-risk species in an area – a tragic local extinction. Australia should begin targeted vaccination of threatened birds. It should also urgently develop a strategy for seals and sea lions, rather than waiting until thousands are dead. A policy exists, but action remains too cautious Australia has a national policy that allows emergency vaccination of rare, protected and valuable birds, including animals in zoos, sanctuaries, breeding programs and some managed wild populations. The government has also purchased an inactivated H5 vaccine – containing no live virus – and is running pilot studies in captive non-poultry birds. This is important groundwork, but not yet a public program comparable with New Zealand’s ambitious and proactive approach to vaccinate five of the country’s rarest birds before the arrival of H5N1. Australian zoos and sanctuaries have received funding to strengthen biosecurity and captive “insurance populations”. Pilot vaccinations are underway, but the government has not announced which threatened species will receive wider vaccination, where, or when. More importantly, the policy excludes non-avian (bird) species, meaning marine mammals are not considered despite their known vulnerability to H5N1. No plans have been announced to the public for Australian vaccination trials for seals or sea lions. What overseas programs show New Zealand prepared before H5N1 arrived. After species-specific trials, it began vaccinating about 300 core breeding birds of rare species, including kākāpō, takahē and black stilts. These are captive or closely managed populations whose individuals can be found, vaccinated twice and monitored. The United States acted after H5N1 killed 21 critically endangered California condors. By October 2024, 207 captive and free-flying condors had been vaccinated. The vaccine was judged safe, although two birds had treatable adverse reactions. France has conducted a vaccine trial in wild king penguin chicks on the French sub-Antarctic island of Crozet. The vaccine produced strong, virus-neutralising antibodies without detected adverse effects. These programs do not prove vaccination will prevent every infection. But it could lessen severe disease and reduce the number of animals that die in threatened populations. The marine mammals most at risk are the sea lion, fur seal and elephant seal, while the Tasmanian devil and eastern quoll (pictured) are the highest-risk species on land. Rexness/flickr, CC BY Which species should Australia vaccinate? Broadscale vaccination of free-ranging wildlife is unrealistic. Most H5 vaccines require two doses, and most wildlife is difficult to capture once, let alone being recaptured for a booster and blood test. The best candidates are small populations of at-risk species that are either easily accessible or already under management. For example, threatened birds in zoos or breeding centres, or small, known colonies with tracking or regular handling. On Tuesday, the Australian government released a list of at-risk species, that showed almost one-in-five Australian bird and mammal species is at high, very high or extreme risk from the virus. Five bird species are at extreme risk – the Christmas Island frigate bird, Houtman albatross, Herald petrel, imperial shag on Heard Island and imperial shag on Macquarie Island. The marine mammals most at risk are the sea lion, fur seal and elephant seal, while the Tasmanian devil and eastern quoll are the highest risk species on land. Decisions must balance extinction risk, exposure to the virus, cost, vaccine performance, whether enough animals can be reached, and whether capture would cause unacceptable stress. Vaccination must sit alongside existing biosecurity, surveillance and conservation measures – not replace them. Australia needs a seal plan H5N1 has decimated seal and sea lion populations across South America and the Southern Ocean. More than 17,000 southern elephant seal pups were killed in Argentina in 2023. An estimated 13,359 pups died at the Australian sub-Antarctic Heard Island in 2025, believed to be from the virus. Southern elephant seals were listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List in April, in part because of the catastrophic mortality caused by bird flu. It will take decades for these populations to recover. Australia’s most vulnerable seals include the endangered Australian sea lion, Australian and long-nosed fur seals, and southern elephant seals. H5N1-positive terns have already been found at Seal Bay on Kangaroo Island, home to a major Australian sea lion breeding colony. Southern elephant seals have a large breeding colony on Australia’s sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, which remains free of H5N1 at this time. There is currently no bird flu vaccine designed specifically for marine mammals. A United States trial aimed at protecting endangered Hawaiian monk seals found a vaccine developed for cattle was safe in northern elephant seals and produced measurable antibodies. This was the closest comparable species for which a safe, conditionally licensed vaccine was available. Developing and approving a separate vaccine for every wildlife species is costly and time-consuming, so conservation programs commonly adapt vaccines already approved for domestic animals. Now is the time to act Australia should identify priority seal colonies now, trial candidate vaccines in a suitable surrogate species and plan how vaccination could be deployed. We should not wait to learn how susceptible these animals are by watching more mass deaths unfold. Vaccination is not a silver bullet. But when a disease can erase years of conservation work in weeks, we should not wait for perfect certainty. It’s time to act before catastrophe. papers.title: Genetic determinants of cell- and egg-preferred replication in H3N2 canine influenza virus.
papers.abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

papers.title: Epidemiology, trends and determinants of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 positivity among severe acute respiratory infection patients in Cambodia, 2020-2024: a hospital-based retrospective cross-sectional surveillance data analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe the epidemiological pattern, temporal trends of influenza and SARS-CoV-2, and determinants of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI)-confirmed positivity among patients hospitalised with SARI in Cambodia. DESIGN: A hospital-based retrospective cross-sectional surveillance data analysis using national sentinel SARI surveillance data collected from 2020 to 2024. SETTING: Nine SARI sentinel hospitals are located across Cambodia. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 16 739 hospitalised patients who met the SARI case definition. MEASURE: SARI-confirmed positivity defines all SARI cases with laboratory-confirmed influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infections as the main outcome measure. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were performed, followed by multivariate logistic regression to identify factors associated with SARI-confirmed positivity. RESULTS: Among 16 739 SARI cases, median age in years was 16 (IQR=59), with 54.6% being male; 13.5% were laboratory-confirmed for influenza or SARS-CoV-2. High mortality rate in 2021. A(H3N2) dominated in 2020, followed by widespread SARS-CoV-2 circulation in 2021. In 2022, SARS-CoV-2 co-circulated with A(H3N2) and influenza B (Victoria). A(H1N1)pdm became the predominant strain in 2023 as SARS-CoV-2 and A(H3N2) declined. In 2024, A(H3N2) again led circulation, with B(Victoria) and SARS-CoV-2 also detected. Sporadic A(H5N1) cases began appearing in late 2023. Multivariable analysis indicated higher odds of SARI-confirmed positivity among children aged 5-14 years (adjusted OR (aOR)=1.85; 95% CI 1.47 to 2.31) and adults 50-64 years (aOR=1.36; 95% CI 1.15 to 1.60) compared with adults 25-49 years, during the rainy season (aOR=2.09; 95% CI 1.89 to 2.32) and among patients in Phnom Penh compared with other regions (p<0.001). Influenza detection markedly increased from 2022 to 2024 following the decline observed during the COVID-19 pandemic. CONCLUSION: These results indicate that there was an increase in SARI trends over the periods and the changing influenza subtypes circulating each year, along with a high mortality rate during the Delta variant COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia. Age, region, year and season were significant factors associated with SARI-confirmed positivity. Targeted interventions and preventive measures should be prioritised for specific high-risk groups.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述柬埔寨住院的 SARI 患者的流行病学模式、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的时间趋势以及严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 确诊阳性的决定因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用2020年至2024年收集的国家哨点SARI 监测数据进行了以医院为基础的回顾性横断面监测数据分析,涉及柬埔寨全国9家SARI哨点医院以及总共16,739名符合SARI病例定义的住院患者。
elements_zh.methods: 进行描述性和双变量分析,然后进行多变量逻辑回归以确定与 SARI 确认的阳性相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 16,739 例 SARI 病例中,13.5% 经实验室确诊为流感或 SARS-CoV-2。多变量分析表明,雨季期间,与 25-49 岁成人相比,5-14 岁儿童(调整后 OR (aOR)=1.85;95% CI 1.47 至 2.31)和 50-64 岁成人(aOR=1.36;95% CI 1.15 至 1.60)SARI 确诊阳性的几率更高(aOR=2.09;95% CI 1.89 至 2.32)以及金边患者与其他地区的患者相比(p<0.001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了每年流行的流感亚型的变化以及与 SARI 确诊阳性相关的重要因素,包括年龄、地区、年份和季节。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为雨季期间和金边的特定高危群体,特别是 50-64 岁的儿童和成人提供有针对性的干预和预防措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对 监测 数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差并限制研究结果的普遍性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Neutralizing and protective monoclonal antibodies identify antigenic sites in influenza H7 hemagglutinin and select for amino acid substitutions rarely observed at the global level.
papers.abstract: Avian influenza viruses of the H7 subtype infect a variety of avian as well as mammalian species, and a better understanding of H7 virus antigenicity and immunogenicity is vital to the development of effective countermeasures for a potential H7 pandemic threat. We have developed a diverse panel of murine monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to the H7 hemagglutinin (HA) and characterized these mAbs for the HA epitope(s) that they bind, their neutralizing activity in vitro against several strains of H7, and their ability to provide protection against virus challenge in vivo . The majority of the isolated mAbs recognized antigenic sites A and B on the globular head of the influenza HA, but mAbs were also isolated to non-canonical sites on HA. Escape viruses generated against the mAbs were used to further define the antigenic sites on the H7 HA, and notably, we find that most amino acid substitutions identified in these escape viruses are rare at the global level. Finally, we used a polyclonal antibody generated by virus infection to assess whether antibody binding and neutralization were impacted by individual amino acid substitutions in the HA of escape viruses generated by the mAbs. The results showed that all of the escape viruses, each of which carried a single amino acid substitution, were still effectively neutralized by polyclonal antibodies, suggesting that the antibody response to H7 infection was broad and redundant.IMPORTANCEInfluenza H7 viruses infect a variety of avian and mammalian species, and present a potential threat to human health. We used a panel of murine monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to facilitate the identification of important protective epitopes on the H7 hemagglutinin (HA). While most of the antibodies bind to antigenic sites A and B on the H7 HA that correspond to well-characterized cognate sites on influenza H3, some antibodies appear to recognize new epitopes in HA distinct from those known antigenic sites. We also identified amino acid substitutions in escape viruses selected by these mAbs and evaluated their impact in the context of polyclonal responses and natural H7 virus evolution over a >60-year period. Taken together, the results add to our understanding of influenza H7 virus antigenicity and immunogenicity, and may have positive implications for successful H7 vaccine development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to better understand the antigenicity and immunogenicity of H7 avian influenza viruses to inform pandemic preparedness and vaccine development against a potential H7 pandemic threat.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a panel of murine monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the H7 hemagglutinin (HA) and characterized their binding, neutralizing activity, and protective capacity against H7 strains in vitro and in vivo.
analysis.methods: Murine monoclonal antibodies were isolated and mapped to antigenic sites on the H7 HA, including canonical sites A and B and non-canonical sites. Escape viruses were generated to identify amino acid substitutions affecting antibody binding, and their impact was assessed using polyclonal antibodies from virus infection.
analysis.main_results: Escape viruses carrying single amino acid substitutions in HA were effectively neutralized by polyclonal antibodies, indicating a broad and redundant antibody response to H7 infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that most amino acid substitutions selected by mAbs are rare globally, suggesting that natural H7 evolution may not readily evade polyclonal responses, which is novel for H7 antigenicity mapping.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform H7 vaccine design by identifying conserved protective epitopes and guiding the selection of antigens that minimize escape potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on murine mAbs and in vitro/in vivo models, which may not fully recapitulate human immune responses, limiting generalizability to human infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antigenicity and immunogenicity of H7 avian influenza viruses by developing murine monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the H7 hemagglutinin (HA). The authors mapped mAbs to antigenic sites, including canonical and non-canonical epitopes, and generated escape viruses to identify amino acid substitutions affecting antibody binding. Notably, escape viruses with single substitutions were still neutralized by polyclonal antibodies, indicating broad and redundant immune responses. The findings suggest that natural H7 evolution rarely selects for substitutions that evade polyclonal neutralization, which may have positive implications for H7 vaccine development by informing the selection of conserved protective epitopes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了更好地了解 H7 禽流感 病毒的抗原性和免疫原性的需要,以便为大流行准备和针对潜在 H7 大流行威胁的 疫苗 开发提供信息。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一组针对 H7 血凝素 (HA) 的鼠单克隆抗体 (mAb),并在体外和体内表征了它们对 H7 菌株的结合、中和活性和保护能力。
elements_zh.methods: 分离鼠单克隆抗体并定位到 H7 HA 上的抗原位点,包括典型位点 A 和 B 以及非典型位点。产生逃逸病毒是为了识别影响抗体结合的氨基酸取代,并使用病毒感染的多克隆抗体评估其影响。
elements_zh.main_results: HA 中携带单个氨基酸取代的逃逸病毒可被多克隆抗体有效中和,表明对 H7 感染有广泛且冗余的抗体反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,mAb 选择的大多数氨基酸取代在全球范围内都是罕见的,这表明天然 H7 进化 可能不容易逃避多克隆反应,这对于 H7 抗原性图谱来说是新颖的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以通过识别保守的保护性表位并指导选择最大限度地减少逃逸可能性的抗原来为 H7 疫苗 设计提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于鼠类单克隆抗体和体外/体内模型,这些模型可能无法完全概括人类 免疫应答,从而限制了对人类感染的普遍性。

papers.abstract_zh: H7 亚型的 禽流感 病毒可感染多种鸟类和哺乳动物,更好地了解 H7 病毒抗原性和免疫原性对于针对潜在的 H7 大流行威胁制定有效对策至关重要。我们开发了针对 H7 血凝素 (HA) 的多种鼠单克隆抗体 (mAb),并表征了这些 mAb 所结合的 HA 表位、它们针对多种 H7 毒株的体外中和活性,以及​​它们在体内提供针对病毒攻击的保护的能力。大多数分离的 mAb 识别流感 HA 球状头部上的抗原位点 A 和 B,但 mAb 也分离到 HA 上的非规范位点。针对 mAb 生成的逃逸病毒用于进一步定义 H7 HA 上的抗原位点,值得注意的是,我们发现这些逃逸病毒中发现的大多数氨基酸取代在全球水平上都是罕见的。最后,我们使用病毒感染产生的多克隆抗体来评估抗体结合和中和是否受到单克隆抗体产生的逃逸病毒 HA 中单个氨基酸取代的影响。结果表明,所有逃逸病毒(每种病毒均携带单个氨基酸取代)仍可被多克隆抗体有效中和,这表明对 H7 感染的抗体反应是广泛且冗余的。重要性 H7 流感病毒感染多种鸟类和哺乳动物物种,并对人类健康构成潜在威胁。我们使用一组鼠单克隆抗体 (mAb) 来促进 H7 血凝素 (HA) 上重要保护性表位的识别。虽然大多数抗体与 H7 HA 上的抗原位点 A 和 B 结合,这些抗原位点对应于 H3 流感病毒上已明确表征的同源位点,但一些抗体似乎可以识别 HA 中不同于那些已知抗原位点的新表位。我们还鉴定了这些 mAb 选择的逃逸病毒中的氨基酸取代,并评估了它们在超过 60 年的时间里对多克隆反应和天然 H7 病毒 进化 的影响。总而言之,这些结果增加了我们对 H7 流感病毒抗原性和免疫原性的理解,并可能对 H7 疫苗 的成功开发产生积极影响。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了更好地了解 H7 禽流感 病毒的抗原性和免疫原性的需要,以便为大流行准备和针对潜在 H7 大流行威胁的 疫苗 开发提供信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究开发了一组针对 H7 血凝素 (HA) 的鼠单克隆抗体 (mAb),并在体外和体内表征了它们对 H7 菌株的结合、中和活性和保护能力。
analysis_zh.methods: 分离鼠单克隆抗体并定位到 H7 HA 上的抗原位点,包括典型位点 A 和 B 以及非典型位点。产生逃逸病毒是为了识别影响抗体结合的氨基酸取代,并使用病毒感染的多克隆抗体评估其影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: HA 中携带单个氨基酸取代的逃逸病毒可被多克隆抗体有效中和,表明对 H7 感染有广泛且冗余的抗体反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,mAb 选择的大多数氨基酸取代在全球范围内都是罕见的,这表明天然 H7 进化 可能不容易逃避多克隆反应,这对于 H7 抗原性图谱来说是新颖的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果可以通过识别保守的保护性表位并指导选择最大限度地减少逃逸可能性的抗原来为 H7 疫苗 设计提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于鼠类单克隆抗体和体外/体内模型,这些模型可能无法完全概括人类 免疫应答,从而限制了对人类感染的普遍性。

papers.title: The One Health Blind Spot at the Human‒Animal Interface in US Influenza Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Novel influenza A viruses have cost thousands of lives and billions of dollars of economic losses in the 21st century, and 2 of the past 4 pandemic influenza A viruses likely originated in animal populations on the North American continent. Despite this, the human and veterinary influenza surveillance systems in the United States are poorly connected and have fallen short of congressional mandates for data sharing and interoperability. This places the United States in a reactive posture that is focused on containment of outbreaks that have already occurred rather than proactive surveillance and prevention. The significant investments in surveillance infrastructure and genomic technologies spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic, along with the new National One Health Framework, present a unique opportunity to modernize influenza surveillance with a greater emphasis on the interconnectedness of human and animal health. However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease significantly as pandemic-era funding sunsets. Continuing investments into novel surveillance technologies have been critical in addressing the recent H5N1 influenza outbreaks and will be critical to prevent future economic losses and losses of both human and animal life. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(8):1220-1228. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308445).

papers.abstract_zh: 新型甲型流感病毒在 21 世纪造成了数千人的生命和数十亿美元的经济损失,过去 4 次大流行甲型流感病毒中有 2 次可能起源于北美大陆的动物种群。尽管如此,美国的人类和兽用流感 监测 系统连接较差,并且未达到国会对数据共享和互操作性的要求。这使美国处于一种被动的姿态,重点是遏制已经发生的暴发,而不是积极主动的暴发和预防。COVID-19 大流行推动了对 监测 基础设施和基因组技术的重大投资,以及新的国家统一健康框架,为实现流感 监测 现代化提供了独特的机会,同时更加强调人类和动物健康的相互联系。然而,随着大流行时代资金的退出,增强型 监测 的资金将大幅减少。对新型 监测 技术的持续投资对于解决最近的 H5N1 流感 暴发 至关重要,对于防止未来的经济损失以及人类和动物生命的损失也至关重要。(《美国公共卫生杂志》。2026;116(8):1220-1228。https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308445)。

papers.title: Revisiting Animal Reservoirs of Hantavirus and Other Zoonotic Viruses on Cruise Ships: Impact and Prevention
papers.abstract: The sustained growth of international maritime tourism and the expansion of the cruise industry have increased the importance of emerging zoonotic diseases as a significant challenge to global public health. Cruise ships constitute complex epidemiological settings characterized by high population density, rapid international mobility, and constant interaction between humans, animals, and coastal environments, factors that favor the introduction and spread of emerging infectious agents. Among the main threats are hantaviruses and other zoonotic viruses, such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, yellow fever, and avian influenza, which are associated with animal reservoirs and vectors present in ports, tourist destinations, and tropical ecosystems. This review examines the ecology of animal reservoirs of hantaviruses and other zoonotic pathogens relevant to maritime tourism, including peri-urban rodents, bats, migratory birds, and other mammals. papers.title: A GIS-based framework for standardized environmental characterization in One-Health surveillance: a case study of HPAI monitoring in wetlands
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) panzootic caused by H5 viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b is constantly re-shaping disease ecology in terms of spatio-temporal spread and host spectrum. Because of this, there is an increasing need to complement traditional surveillance methods with approaches that consider environmental factors into epidemiological interpretation. Although environmental surveillance is increasingly recognized within a One Health framework, environmental descriptors are not always consistently structured, underscoring the importance of adopting standardized approaches for their collection and management. Method A GIS-based framework was developed to standardize environmental characterization of HPAI surveillance sites. Environmental data were collected at nine wetlands in north-eastern Italy, using ESRI field map tool, synchronised through ArcGIS online. Data were validated with field-base ground truthing, stored in a spatial relational database and aggregated into harmonised site-specific descriptors, suitable for epidemiological modelling and analyses. Results This study introduces a GIS-based framework designed to standardize how environmental features are recorded at sampling sites for HPAI surveillance. The workflow turns different types of field observations into organized geographical datasets that can be analysed. When used at wetland surveillance sites in north-eastern Italy, this framework produced consistent environmental data and standardized records for each site. Conclusions The workflow combines mobile GIS tools (ESRI Field Maps), ArcGIS Online/Pro, and a PostGIS database to create standardized outputs for epidemiological analysis. This setup creates a reliable connection between field ecology, spatial data infrastructures, and disease risk analysis.

papers.title_zh: 基于 GIS 的 One-Health 监测 标准化环境特征框架:湿地高致病性禽流感监测案例研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background The Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) panzootic caused by H5 viruses of clade 2.3.4.4b is constantly re-shaping disease ecology in terms of spatio-temporal spread and host spectrum. Because of this, there is an increasing need to complement traditional surveillance methods with approaches that consider environmental factors into epidemiological interpretation. Although environmental surveillance is increasingly recognized within a One Health framework, environmental descriptors are not always consistently structured, underscoring the importance of adopting standardized approaches for their collection and management. Method A GIS-based framework was developed to standardize environmental characterization of HPAI surveillance sites. Environmental data were collected at nine wetlands in north-eastern Italy, using ESRI field map tool, synchronised through ArcGIS online. Data were validated with field-base ground truthing, stored in a spatial relational database and aggregated into harmonised site-specific descriptors, suitable for epidemiological modelling and analyses. Results This study introduces a GIS-based framework designed to standardize how environmental features are recorded at sampling sites for HPAI surveillance. The workflow turns different types of field observations into organized geographical datasets that can be analysed. When used at wetland surveillance sites in north-eastern Italy, this framework produced consistent environmental data and standardized records for each site. Conclusions The workflow combines mobile GIS tools (ESRI Field Maps), ArcGIS Online/Pro, and a PostGIS database to create standardized outputs for epidemiological analysis. This setup creates a reliable connection between field ecology, spatial data infrastructures, and disease risk analysis.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 由分支 2.3.4.4b 的 H5 病毒引起的 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 动物疫病在时空传播和 宿主 谱方面不断重塑疾病生态。因此,越来越需要用将环境因素纳入流行病学解释的方法来补充传统的 监测 方法。尽管环境 监测 在“同一个健康”框架内得到越来越多的认可,但环境描述符的结构并不总是一致,这强调了采用标准化方法进行收集和管理的重要性。方法 开发了基于 GIS 的框架来标准化 HPAI 监测 场地的环境特征。使用 ESRI 现场地图工具收集意大利东北部的九个湿地的环境数据,并通过 ArcGIS Online 同步。数据通过实地地面实况验证,存储在空间关系数据库中,并汇总成统一的特定地点描述符,适合流行病学建模和分析。结果本研究引入了一个基于 GIS 的框架,旨在标准化 HPAI 监测 采样点环境特征的记录方式。该工作流程将不同类型的现场观察转化为可分析的有组织的地理数据集。当在意大利东北部的湿地 监测 站点使用时,该框架为每个站点生成了一致的环境数据和标准化记录。结论 该工作流程结合了移动 GIS 工具(ESRI Field Maps)、ArcGIS Online/Pro 和 PostGIS 数据库,为流行病学分析创建标准化输出。这种设置在野外生态学、空间数据基础设施和疾病风险分析之间建立了可靠的联系。

papers.title: Pathogen prevalence and health risks in European backyard poultry: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Backyard poultry keeping has expanded across Europe, driven by increasing interest in locally produced eggs and meat. However, these small and often unregistered flocks may operate with limited veterinary supervision and variable biosecurity, creating opportunities for contact between domestic birds, commercial poultry, wildlife, and humans. Despite these concerns, evidence on pathogen occurrence in European backyard poultry systems remains scattered and heterogeneous. This scoping review aimed to identify and synthesize the available evidence on pathogens reported in European backyard poultry flocks. Specifically, it sought to: (i) map reported occurrences of parasitic, bacterial, and viral pathogens; (ii) describe the diagnostic methods used; (iii) summarize factors associated with pathogen detection or transmission as reported in the included studies; and (iv) highlight methodological gaps and priorities for future surveillance and research. The review was conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Searches were performed in PubMed, CAB Abstracts, and Scopus up to July 2024. Studies conducted in Europe and focusing on backyard or small-scale poultry flocks were eligible if they reported pathogen occurrence, diagnostic methods, or associated factors. Thirty-three studies from 17 European countries met the inclusion criteria. Data extracted included study design, flock characteristics, pathogens investigated, diagnostic approaches, reported occurrence or prevalence values, and associated factors. This review shows that a wide range of parasitic, bacterial, and viral pathogens has been reported in European backyard poultry flocks, including Eimeria spp., Dermanyssus gallinae , Mycoplasma gallisepticum , Salmonella spp., avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, and Marek’s disease virus. Some studies reported high pathogen detection frequencies, and several associated factors were described, including outdoor access, multispecies keeping, contact with wild birds, and limited biosecurity. However, the evidence base remains fragmented due to uneven geographical coverage, predominantly cross-sectional study designs, frequent use of convenience sampling, heterogeneous diagnostic methods, and differences in sampling units. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as a mapping of reported pathogen occurrence and associated factors, rather than as estimates of true European prevalence or evidence of reservoir status. Improved surveillance, harmonized diagnostic protocols, and longitudinal studies are needed to better characterize pathogen circulation and its implications for animal and public health within a One Health framework.

Studies conducted in Europe and focusing on backyard or small-scale poultry flocks were eligible if they reported pathogen occurrence, diagnostic methods, or associated factors. Thirty-three studies from 17 European countries met the inclusion criteria. Data extracted included study design, flock characteristics, pathogens investigated, diagnostic approaches, reported occurrence or prevalence values, and associated factors. This review shows that a wide range of parasitic, bacterial, and viral pathogens has been reported in European backyard poultry flocks, including Eimeria spp., Dermanyssus gallinae , Mycoplasma gallisepticum , Salmonella spp., avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, and Marek’s disease virus. Some studies reported high pathogen detection frequencies, and several associated factors were described, including outdoor access, multispecies keeping, contact with wild birds, and limited biosecurity. However, the evidence base remains fragmented due to uneven geographical coverage, predominantly cross-sectional study designs, frequent use of convenience sampling, heterogeneous diagnostic methods, and differences in sampling units. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as a mapping of reported pathogen occurrence and associated factors, rather than as estimates of true European prevalence or evidence of reservoir status. Improved surveillance, harmonized diagnostic protocols, and longitudinal studies are needed to better characterize pathogen circulation and its implications for animal and public health within a One Health framework.

papers.title: BIOSECURITY PRACTICES AND RISK PERCEPTION IN SUBSISTENCE POULTRY SYSTEMS AT THE WILDLIFE–DOMESTIC INTERFACE IN MARANHÃO, BRAZIL
papers.abstract: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) represents a significant threat to animal health, public health, and food security, particularly in areas where there is an interface between migratory wild birds and subsistence domestic poultry systems. Under such conditions, weaknesses in biosecurity and limited access to information and veterinary services may increase the risk of virus introduction and dissemination. The objective of this study was to evaluate management and biosecurity practices, risk perception, and receptiveness to preventive actions in subsistence poultry systems located around the migratory site of Panaquatira, Maranhão, Brazil. A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted between January and June 2025 through the application of a structured questionnaire to 70 poultry keepers. The analyzed variables included socioeconomic profile, flock characteristics, sanitary practices, knowledge about migratory birds and avian influenza, and interest in educational strategies. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and exploratory association analyses. A predominance of keepers with low formal education was observed, along with multispecies flocks mainly intended for self-consumption and limited adoption of basic biosecurity measures. Although many respondents reported recognizing signs of illness in birds, the actions taken were primarily based on personal experience, with low demand for veterinary assistance and limited notification to official services. Knowledge regarding the epidemiological role of migratory birds was restricted. Conversely, a high level of receptiveness to technical guidance and sanitary education initiatives was observed. The results indicate the existence of relevant vulnerabilities for HPAI prevention in subsistence systems located in ecologically sensitive areas, but also highlight opportunities to strengthen participatory surveillance and prevention through educational interventions adapted to the local context.
authors: Carla Janaína Rebouças Marques do Rosário
papers.journal: Preventive Veterinary Medicine Regional Studies and Reports

It highlights the vulnerability of these systems to Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) due to low formal education among poultry keepers, multispecies flocks primarily for self-consumption, and limited adoption of biosecurity measures. Although many respondents reported recognizing signs of illness in birds, the actions taken were primarily based on personal experience, with low demand for veterinary assistance and limited notification to official services. Knowledge regarding the epidemiological role of migratory birds was restricted. Conversely, a high level of receptiveness to technical guidance and sanitary education initiatives was observed. The results indicate the existence of relevant vulnerabilities for HPAI prevention in subsistence systems located in ecologically sensitive areas, but also highlight opportunities to strengthen participatory surveillance and prevention through educational interventions adapted to the local context.

papers.title: AFB1 promotes H3N8 replication in chickens by impairing gut colonization of protective segmented filamentous bacteria
papers.abstract: Abstract AFB1, a common feed mycotoxin, can worsen viral infections. While H3N8 avian influenza mainly affects birds and can harm gut health, the combined impact of AFB1 and H3N8 infection on poultry intestines remains unknown. We show that environmentally relevant AFB1 levels (25–100 μg/kg) significantly enhance H3N8 replication in vitro and in vivo. Integrated histopathological, microbiome, and metabolomic analyses revealed AFB1-induced gut barrier dysfunction and specific depletion of beneficial bacteria (Eubacterium, Subdoligranulum), correlating with reduced dodecanedioic acid. Critically, AFB1 impaired ileal colonization of segmented filamentous bacteria (SFB), creating a permissive environment for viral propagation. Intervention with SFB supplementation reversed AFB1-mediated enhancement of H3N8 infection. Mechanistically, AFB1 disrupts intestinal homeostasis by compromising mucosal integrity and SFB colonization, thereby amplifying H3N8 pathogenesis. These findings establish a novel mycotoxin-virus interaction axis mediated through gut dysbiosis, underscoring the urgent need for AFB1 control strategies in poultry production to mitigate influenza risks.
